stem: A client with long-standing type 2 diabetes has persistent resting tachycardia. When standing, the client becomes lightheaded and the blood pressure falls; the client also reports urinary retention. After other acute causes are excluded, which complication best explains this multisystem pattern?

options.A: Diabetic autonomic neuropathy affecting cardiovascular and genitourinary autonomic function
options.B: Distal symmetric peripheral neuropathy limited primarily to somatic sensory nerves
options.C: Acute volume depletion alone, which explains both the chronic urinary retention and the autonomic findings
options.D: Normal aging, because these findings are expected when diabetes has been present for many years

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care list resting tachycardia and orthostatic hypotension among manifestations of cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy and neurogenic bladder/urinary dysfunction among manifestations of diabetic autonomic neuropathy. A multisystem pattern involving cardiovascular and genitourinary autonomic function is therefore consistent with diabetic autonomic neuropathy once other causes are considered. B can cause distal sensory loss, burning, and loss of protective sensation but does not explain this combined autonomic cardiovascular and bladder pattern. C may cause orthostatic symptoms and tachycardia but does not adequately explain chronic urinary retention in this scenario. D is unsafe because these findings are not simply expected normal aging.
educational_objective: Recognize diabetic autonomic neuropathy when long-standing diabetes is accompanied by a multisystem autonomic pattern such as resting tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, and neurogenic bladder symptoms after other causes are considered.
source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
source_document_title: Retinopathy, Neuropathy, and Foot Care: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
source_locator: Diabetic Autonomic Neuropathy; Cardiovascular Autonomic Neuropathy; Recommendation 12.19 — major manifestations include resting tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, gastrointestinal and genitourinary dysfunction including neurogenic bladder; autonomic symptoms/signs warrant assessment and exclusion of other causes
source_claim_supported: Diabetic autonomic neuropathy can affect multiple organ systems; current ADA guidance identifies resting tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, and neurogenic bladder/urinary dysfunction as recognized manifestations, with evaluation for other causes as appropriate.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation; identify pathophysiology and manifestations of chronic complications and recognize changes requiring intervention
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source label-recognition item into a multisystem clinical differential. The final stem uses the ADA-supported cardiovascular and genitourinary autonomic manifestations, specifies that other acute causes have been excluded to reduce second-answer risk, and replaces vague bladder dysfunction with urinary retention consistent with neurogenic bladder.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.clinical_category: diabetic autonomic neuropathy / cardiovascular and genitourinary autonomic dysfunction
audit_findings.source_audit: Verified directly against ADA Standards of Care 2026 Section 12. The current source explicitly lists resting tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, and neurogenic bladder among diabetic autonomic neuropathy manifestations.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: The stem combines three directly supported autonomic findings and avoids assigning the diagnosis until other acute causes have been considered. No unsupported blood-pressure threshold or heart-rate cutoff is introduced.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; it explains the combined cardiovascular and genitourinary autonomic pattern.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; distal symmetric peripheral neuropathy is primarily somatic sensory and does not explain the full autonomic cluster.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; acute volume depletion may contribute to orthostatic findings but does not best explain chronic urinary retention plus the full multisystem pattern.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; these findings should not be dismissed as normal aging.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A accounts for all stated chronic multisystem findings after other acute causes are excluded.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are plausible clinical explanations at a similar level of specificity.
audit_findings.blueprint: Physiological Adaptation is appropriate because the item tests recognition of a chronic multisystem complication and its pathophysiologic manifestations.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked autonomic-neuropathy manifestations, orthostatic differential, volume-depletion confounding, urinary-retention specificity, distal symmetric neuropathy overlap, absence of unsupported numeric thresholds, difficulty level, and second-answer risk. No unresolved conflict remained.
